newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alumbrera sells copper to LG Metals.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alumbrera sells copper to LG Metals.

text.p: Argentina's Minera Alumbrera Ltd said Monday it will fix smelting charges with South Korea's LG Metals Corp for 100,000 tonnes of its copper concentrates in the next international negotiating round.

"Our first deliveries will be in the second half of calendar '97, so I guess we will become involved in the next round of negotiations internationally," Minera Alumbrera president Peter Freund told reporters.

Freund was speaking in Buenos Aires after signing a contract with LG Metals to supply 100,000 tonnes of copper and gold concentrates between 1998 and 2007. Minera Alumbrera estimated the value of the contract at $800 million.
Referring to how treatment and refining terms will be set, Freund said, "It is a normal frame contract arrangement where those things will be negotiated on a market basis each year."

He said that Minera Alumbrera had letters of intent for about four-fifths of its concentrate output. But he added, "This is the first in the process of turning those letters of intent into firm frame contracts."

Freund said there were about four other concentrates sales negotiations all running neck and neck in the race to be the next signing. He declined to identify the companies involved but said they were from Spain, Germany and Canada.
The Bajo de la Alumbrera mine is owned 50 percent by Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd, and 25 percent each by North Ltd, of Australia, and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd.
The $900-million mine is being built in Argentina's northwestern province of Catamarca and is set to produce 180,000 tonnes of copper and 20 tonnes of gold a year for at least 20 years.
